{"id": "8316fcc3-992a-46ab-842b-dc43ba848ddd", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "These three questions sit outside anything I can pull from AWS APIs or your agent space — and I want to be upfront about that rather than guess:

- **Who is affected** needs a dependency/service map tying this cluster to downstream consumers. You mentioned none exists, and I don't have a topology source to build one from scratch right now.
- **What this is costing us** needs a revenue-per-minute figure, which isn't something infrastructure telemetry can tell me. Without it, I can't translate 20 minutes of degradation into a dollar figure.
- **Compliance reporting deadlines** (e.g., SLA/regulatory incident reporting windows) live in legal/compliance documentation, not infrastructure — I have no access to that.

What I *can* do right now on the technical side: look at the Aurora cluster itself — what "degraded" means concretely (failover event, CPU/connections/replica lag, recent parameter or infra changes), and which resources reference it (e.g., via CloudFormation stacks, security groups, or connection strings in logs) to get a partial picture of blast radius even without a formal dependency map.

If that's useful, tell me the cluster identifier (and region/account if you have more than one), and I'll start pulling the degradation signal and any discoverable callers.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
